messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — we need a final pass on the metric taxonomy coming out of runtime for the sprint planning doc. Can runtime owners confirm label names and expected cardinalities by EOD Friday?

sam: @maya noted. We can produce the label list, but need clarity on which labels are allowed on high-cardinality user-facing metrics vs billing/telemetry only.

frank: Short proposal: keep per-request Prom metrics with low-cardinality labels only (env, region, route_id, model_family). Anything customer-specific (customer_id, team_id) goes into usage/billing metrics that are aggregated, or into traces/logs.

jen: +1 on that. Also prefer snake_case for label names (route_id, model_name, runtime_version) — avoids surprises in dashboards.

olivia: We should also standardize on model identifiers. Runtime currently emits model_name (human) and model_hash (stable). Which should dashboards use?

sam: For dashboards use model_name for readability, model_hash for rollups/joins. But model_name must be a stable token (no timestamps). If ops changes naming, dashboards break. So recommend model_version tag like: model_name=\"gpt4o\", model_version=\"2026-03-01\"

frank: Cardinality concerns: route_id ~ thousands, model_name ~ dozens, customer_id ~ 100k+. Rule of thumb: avoid attaching customer_id to any Prom vector that will be scraped at high QPS.

maya: Agreed. Let's codify:
- Prom metrics that feed dashboards: no customer_id, no full-run ids
- Billing/usage counters: may include customer_id but should be recorded in pre-aggregated form or in a separate metrics namespace
- Traces/logs: include full identifiers for debugging

sam: Example metric we should standardize:
```
redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=\"prod\",route_id=\"chat_v1\",model_name=\"gpt4o\",region=\"us-east-1\"}
```
No customer_id label on that.

jen: Also suggest we stop using both model and model_family inconsistently. Pick model_name + model_family optional. model_family should be low-card and stable (e.g., \"gpt4o-family\").

olivia: For rollout dashboards we need route_version and rollout_tag so we can split p50/p95 by rollout. Those are low-card if we keep tags small.

frank: On OTEL vs Prom labels: OTEL resource attributes often have host-level info. We should map these to Prom labels at scrape time and document the mapping. For example: resource.attributes.service.name -> prometheus label service_name.

maya: Good call. I'll draft a mapping table. Can infra team add a scrubber that drops high-card attrs from Prom relabel config? 

infra-bot: deploy-notice: relabel-config-v2 applied to prod scrapers at 1772345800.

sam: @maya thanks. Once we have the table, platform team will run a cardinality simulation (estimate distinct label values per cardinality window) and flag any metric exceeding threshold.

maya: Threshold proposal: low-card metrics target < 10k series in prod, medium-card < 100k but aggregated, anything >100k needs an alternative recording strategy. Thoughts?

jen: Those numbers seem reasonable. For per-route latency in enterprise tenants, we might need recording rules that aggregate route x region x model only.

olivia: UX ask: consoles need consistent metric names (prefix redwood_) and namespaced sections: latency.*, throughput.*, errors.*, resource.* so product dashboards are discoverable.

frank: +1 on prefix. Suggest metric naming guideline: prefix = redwood_inference, suffix category = latency|requests|tokens, full example: redwood_inference_requests_total, redwood_inference_tokens_produced_total.

maya: OK action items:
1) runtime (sam/frank) publish label list + model_name/version policy by Fri 1772422078
2) eng-platform (maya/jen) produce mapping doc and cardinality thresholds
3) infra (olivia) confirm relabel-scrub rules and provide simulation outputs
4) schedule 30m sync next Tue to sign-off on naming + dashboards

sam: I'll upload a draft to the metrics-notebooks channel later today.

jen: I'll stub dashboard templates for latency and throughput with the proposed labels.

olivia: I'll share a relabel-config and estimated series counts.

maya: Thanks all — this will help the rollout and console UX stay stable. If nobody objects, I'll open the PR with the taxonomy doc Monday morning. :thumbsup:

sam: Sounds good.

frank: Thanks.

infra-bot: meeting-scheduled: metrics-taxonomy-signoff on 1772498400 (Tue) 09:30 UTC."
